contract_clarifications.rule: Leases start immediately at accepted controller issue time; expires_at=issued_at+duration_seconds. No future-start API.

contract_clarifications.source: Parent task message before original scenario sealing; 2026-11-11
contract_clarifications.rule: Desired and closure commands have a5-second TTL. Application is valid only while now<deadline. A timeout is refused with reason deadline; a currently eligible lease may receive a fresh command.

contract_clarifications.source: Parent task message before original scenario sealing; 2026-11-11
contract_clarifications.rule: Fixture-clock rollback returns clock_rollback and preserves domain state. Operational UTC rollback likewise refuses new mutations; reads remain available. Rejection does not promise an audit append.

contract_clarifications.source: Parent task message before original scenario sealing; 2026-11-11
contract_clarifications.rule: Observed external/unattributed revisions, including same-value revisions not explained by an own acknowledgement, suppress all existing leases on that scope and revoke ownership. Cause remains external_unattributed without invented human attribution.

contract_clarifications.source: Parent task message before original scenario sealing; 2026-11-11
contract_clarifications.rule: A new exact-value winner on proven owned state adopts lease and restore policy through no_op_adoption, preserving baseline/fence and device version. An unowned exact-value target is fulfilled_noop and acquires no ownership or baseline.

global_expected_observations: No applied desired target is expired, cancelled, suppressed, superseded, deadline-expired, generation-stale or version-stale at actual application.
A valid conditional closure is a separate action with a new command ID/deadline and surviving ownership proof. It is not counted as executing an expired desired target.
No closure overwrites a newer manual or external decision, including same-value revision events.
Each automatic application has one durable receipt binding unique command ID, scope, deciding lease (or ended lease and closure proof), before/after values, before/after versions and logical time.
A refused delivery is visible with a reason and creates no successful application receipt. Historical successful receipt replay is permitted but cannot execute again.
Only actual device writes advance automatic device versions. Every synthetic manual/external event advances its scope version even if values match.
Fixture time and operational injected-source time are synthetic test inputs, never measured physical latency.
reopen_process means a separately started process using the same durable SQLite file, not only in-memory object reinstantiation.
unresolved_or_nonprescribed: When several guards fail simultaneously, the contract does not order refusal reasons. Such cases require a visible reason and zero application; isolated deadline cases require deadline.
Exact public API method names, JSON output layout, resolver-generation numeric values and receipt IDs are adapter details. Command IDs must remain unique and aliases bind the originals.
Rejected requests preserve durable domain state. Diagnostic counters/events or read-only process metadata are outside same_domain_state_as.
This set does not prescribe migrations, retention, large-installation throughput, hardware behavior, a future-start interface or arbitrary-model accuracy.

cases.title: Compare expiry restores an uninterrupted baseline
cases.invariant: One acknowledged automatic change owns the prior light vector. Expiry closes that ownership through a distinct proved restoration.
cases.failure_if: The light stays leased, expiry replays the expired target, or a restoring receipt lacks baseline/version proof.

cases.title: Leave expiry closes ownership without a write
cases.invariant: Leave preserves the last automatic value while ending ownership.
cases.failure_if: Expiry restores the seed or fabricates a device revision.

cases.title: Priority interruption preserves the original chain baseline
cases.invariant: An eligible loser resumes when its interrupter ends; automatic winner changes retain the original baseline.
cases.failure_if: A never resumes, or final closure restores an intermediate automatic value.

cases.title: Same-time ties use persisted submission sequence
cases.invariant: Equal priority is decided by the later persisted submission even at an identical fixture instant.
cases.failure_if: Earlier A wins the tie, or the losing explanation fails to name B.

cases.title: Later member loses to higher operator priority
cases.invariant: Validated numeric priority dominates submission order.
cases.failure_if: Priority50 member displaces a still-active priority80 operator.

cases.title: Light interruption leaves media ownership independent
cases.invariant: A two-scope request may lose light while continuing to own media. Scope versions and closures are separate.
cases.failure_if: Light-only B changes media or causes media to gain a spurious revision.

cases.title: Manual zero brightness suppresses every old light request
cases.invariant: Brightness zero means the whole off vector and suppresses both light winner and loser; media remains independent.
cases.failure_if: A prior light request returns after manual off, or media is suppressed by a light operation.

cases.title: Same-value manual decision defeats automatic restoration
cases.invariant: A manual event increments version even if the value is unchanged. Value equality alone never proves ownership.
cases.failure_if: Manual60 is treated as a no-op and expiry restores off over it.

cases.title: A new lease takes the intervening manual baseline
cases.invariant: A newly confirmed lease can own a newer manual state. Its baseline cannot be the original seed or an older automatic value.
cases.failure_if: Suppressed A returns, or B closes to off instead of manual25.

cases.title: Manual media pause preserves light restoration
cases.invariant: A manual media event revokes media ownership alone.
cases.failure_if: Expiry overwrites paused media or fails to close independently owned light.

cases.title: Offline pending is never an acknowledgement
cases.invariant: An offline device cannot acknowledge a queued intention. Reconnect after expiry must not execute that intention.
cases.failure_if: A queue label is counted as a write, or reconnect sets60 after expiry.

cases.title: Reconnect applies the current winner instead of queue order
cases.invariant: A current resolver winner overrides queue ordering. An eligible loser can resume only after the winner ends.
cases.failure_if: Old queued A writes during B ownership or reconnect applies both targets.

cases.title: Reconnect observes offline manual change before planning
cases.invariant: Offline device state can differ from the controller's last observation. Reconnect revokes stale ownership before authorizing any target.
cases.failure_if: A stale observed version authorizes restoring off over manual25.

cases.title: Offline same-value manual change prevents loser revival
cases.invariant: A new observed device version suppresses every older lease for that scope, even if the value equals the former winner's value.
cases.failure_if: A returns because the controller missed the same-value manual revision.

cases.title: Separate-process reopen preserves active ownership
cases.invariant: The same SQLite file reopened in another process retains leases, versions, ownership, receipts and logical clock.
cases.failure_if: Only an object is reinstantiated, ownership resets, or a second write repeats an acknowledged command.

cases.title: Expired offline command remains invalid after process restart
cases.invariant: Restart retains time and pending-command validity; it does not turn an unapplied expired lease into ownership.
cases.failure_if: The restarted process applies60 or restores a baseline that was never acquired.

cases.title: Cancelling a winner resumes an unsuppressed loser
cases.invariant: Cancellation removes only its lease; resolution finds the remaining eligible lease before considering closure.
cases.failure_if: Cancelling B closes the chain despite eligible A or erases A.

cases.title: Cancellation invalidates a never-applied desired command
cases.invariant: A queued intention has no acknowledged ownership. Cancellation cannot leave an executable target or a fictitious restore action.
cases.failure_if: Old A applies after cancellation or closure increments a never-changed device.

cases.title: Same target value cannot validate an old resolver generation
cases.invariant: A stale deciding lease is not current merely because its target equals the new winner's target.
cases.failure_if: The superseded A command writes or is silently attributed to B.

cases.title: Duplicate delivery returns a receipt without repeating the write
cases.invariant: Successful command replay is historical receipt replay, including after closure. It cannot execute again.
cases.failure_if: A duplicate increments version, creates another application receipt or returns the device to60 after expiry.

cases.title: Manual race defeats an undelivered expected-version command
cases.invariant: Device application validates version and target eligibility in the same transaction. A manual race must not be overwritten.
cases.failure_if: The delayed command overwrites manual20 or produces a successful application receipt.

cases.title: Desired target cannot execute at exact lease expiry
cases.invariant: A lease is ineligible at now equal to its expiry, even when no prior reconciliation marked it ended.
cases.failure_if: Boundary delivery increments the device or applies the expired desired target.

cases.title: Ended lease can justify fresh closure without replaying its target
cases.invariant: Closure has its own proof and new bounded deadline. It may validly restore the baseline after A's desired target has expired.
cases.failure_if: All actions after lease expiry are rejected, or the closure is represented as replaying expired60.

cases.title: A new winning lease invalidates a queued restoration
cases.invariant: A pending closure is invalid once a new winner exists, even before the new winner writes. With no external change, the ownership chain baseline survives.
cases.failure_if: A's closure flashes off during B ownership, or B later restores an intermediate60 baseline.

cases.title: Same-value manual event invalidates queued restoration
cases.invariant: An old closure cannot rely on equality of values after a manual revision; the new version closes ownership.
cases.failure_if: Queued closure overwrites the manual60 decision with off.

cases.title: Expired closure command needs a fresh safe closure
cases.invariant: A closure command expires at its own deadline. Reconnect may create a different fresh command if the original ownership proof still survives.
cases.failure_if: The expired command executes, or refreshing a safe closure replays an ended desired target.

cases.title: Already matching unowned state is a fulfilled no-op
cases.invariant: An unowned match is fulfilled without ownership, baseline acquisition or fabricated write. Expiry cannot restore an invented baseline.
cases.failure_if: The no-op increases a version, fabricates an application receipt or claims ownership.

cases.title: Fixture-clock rollback refuses mutation and survives reopen
cases.invariant: The declared fixture clock is monotonic and durable. A refused rollback preserves domain state and still permits inspection.
cases.failure_if: Time moves backward, state mutates during rejection, or restart forgets the accepted clock.

cases.title: Exact duplicate ID preserves original sequence and expiry
cases.invariant: An exact duplicate returns the durable original record rather than extending duration, incrementing sequence or creating another command.
cases.failure_if: Retry extends A from10 to12, changes its sequence or repeats its acknowledged write.

cases.title: Conflicting body cannot reuse an existing stable ID
cases.invariant: Once ID A identifies a body, differing targets or duration are refused without changing any domain record.
cases.failure_if: A's body is updated, its expiry changes or rejection partially mutates state.

cases.title: Invalid coupled light vectors are refused without coercion
cases.invariant: Light is a complete valid atomic vector: off/0 or on/integer1..100. Booleans, strings and floats are not coerced to integer brightness.
cases.failure_if: Any malformed vector creates a lease, command, receipt or device revision.

cases.title: Bounds, role and scalar types reject invalid requests
cases.invariant: Role bounds and finite integer inputs are checked before any lease mutation. Validation never coerces strings or booleans.
cases.failure_if: Invalid bounds, fake roles or unsupported room/policy/media values enter the domain.

cases.title: Inclusive valid priority and duration boundaries remain usable
cases.invariant: Priority0, member50, operator100, duration1 and duration86400 are accepted as integer boundaries. Fixture days do not represent wall performance.
cases.failure_if: Boundary values are rejected or the long lease expires at an incorrect instant.

cases.title: Unknown keys and arbitrary executable shapes are refused
cases.invariant: Only the bounded lease schema is executable. Owner/role are supplied by operator context, not request or model JSON.
cases.failure_if: Unknown keys are discarded silently or entity/service/action data can become device operations.

cases.title: Duplicate JSON keys are refused even when values match
cases.invariant: Duplicate detection applies to every JSON object before any typed request is constructed.
cases.failure_if: A parser selects first/last duplicate values or accepts an identical duplicate and creates a lease.

cases.title: Nonfinite JSON numbers never enter durable state
cases.invariant: NaN and infinities are refused; numeric overflow cannot silently become a finite duration or priority.
cases.failure_if: A nonfinite/overflowing number is accepted, coerced or committed partially.

cases.title: Operational UTC rollback refuses a new mutation while reads work
cases.invariant: A synthetic injected UTC source exercises the operational monotonicity guard. It is not a real clock or latency measurement.
cases.failure_if: Backward source time permits B, destroys A, prevents inspection or resets the durable high-water time.

cases.title: Owned no-op successor adopts leave policy without a write
cases.invariant: An owned exact-value winner change transfers deciding lease/policy and preserves the original baseline and fence, without changing the device.
cases.failure_if: B fails to adopt policy or its no-op increments version; final expiry restores off despite B's leave policy.

cases.title: Owned no-op successor can adopt compare policy
cases.invariant: A compare successor controls closure after exact-value ownership adoption, even when the last actual device write came from a leave predecessor.
cases.failure_if: Closure incorrectly uses A's leave policy or no-op adoption fabricates a device write.

cases.title: Unattributed same-value external revision suppresses old leases
cases.invariant: An unexplained observed revision revokes ownership and suppresses all existing scope leases. Its origin stays unknown rather than being assigned a human name.
cases.failure_if: A resumes after the external revision or an invented human identity is recorded for the external event.

cases.title: A timed-out desired command needs a fresh eligible command
cases.invariant: A desired command is invalid at its own5s deadline even while its30s lease is still eligible. A newly planned current command can succeed.
cases.failure_if: The expired command executes, or command timeout incorrectly cancels the still-live lease.
